How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide (with a concrete example) that shows you exactly how to build and execute a **GET** request against the *Device Connector Versions* API on **Cisco Nexus Dashboard v6.3.1**. --- ## 1️⃣ Identify the Endpoint For Nexus Dashboard 6.x the base URL for all APIs is: ``` https:///api/v1/ ``` The specific resource you want – “get information of device connector versions” – lives at: ``` /device_connector_versions ``` So the full endpoint becomes: ``` https:///api/v1/device_connector_versions ``` > **Tip:** Replace `` with your actual host name or IP address (e.g., `nexus.example.com`). --- ## 2️⃣ Gather Authentication Credentials All Nexus Dashboard APIs require a bearer token (JWT). If you don’t already have one, obtain it via the **Login** API: ```http POST /api/v1/login Content-Type: application/json { "username": "", "password": "" } ``` The response will contain a field called `"token"`. Copy that value – you’ll paste it into the `Authorization` header below. --- ## 3️⃣ Build the Request | Element | What to put | |---------|-------------| | **Method** | `GET` | | **URL** | `https:///api/v1/device_connector_versions` | | **Headers** |
  • `Authorization: Bearer `
  • `Accept: application/json`
| | **Query Parameters** | None required for a simple list, but you can filter by `connector_type`, `status`, etc. Example: `?connector_type=iosxr&status=active` | ### Full cURL Example ```bash curl -X GET \ https:///api/v1/device_connector_versions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` ### Full Postman Example 1. **Create a new request** → Set method to **GET**. 2. Paste the full URL into the address bar. 3. Under **Headers**, add: * Key: `Authorization` Value: `Bearer ` * Key: `Accept` Value: `application/json` 4. Click **Send**. --- ## 4️⃣ Inspect the Response A successful call returns HTTP status **200 OK** and a JSON payload similar to: ```json { "data": [ { "id": 101, "name": "IOS-XR", "version": "7.0.3", "status": "active", "last_updated": "2026-06-28T12:34:56Z" }, { "id": 102, "name": "NX-OS", "version": "9.3.5", "status": "deprecated", "last_updated": "2025-11-01T08:20:00Z" } ], "meta": { "total_count": 2, "page": 1, "per_page": 50 } } ``` If you receive a **401 Unauthorized**, double‑check that the token is still valid and that you’re using the correct header format (`Bearer `). --- ## 5️⃣ Automate the Call (Optional) If you’d like to programmatically hit this endpoint from Python, you can use the helper function defined in the toolset: ```python from functions import requests_get response = requests_get( url="https:///api/v1/device_connector_versions", params={}, # Add any query parameters here ) print(response.json()) ``` Make sure you’ve installed the `requests` library (`pip install requests`) and that you pass the proper authentication header inside the function (the tool wrapper handles that for you). --- ## Quick Checklist - [ ] Replace `` with your real host/IP. - [ ] Obtain a fresh JWT via `/login`. - [ ] Use `Authorization: Bearer ` header. - [ ] Send a `GET` request to `/api/v1/device_connector_versions`. - [ ] Verify you get a `200 OK` and a JSON body. That’s all there is to it! Once you have the token and the endpoint, the rest is just standard REST‑style HTTP. Happy querying!
